evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 12288 finite FP16 values with |x| >= 1024 (both signs, up to 64512): kernel output vs FP64 torch.sin max abs error 1.34e-7, zero violations of the 1e-6 tolerance. Only 4 inputs show an FP32-vs-exact q mismatch, and their errors are <= 3.9e-8 (benign: at half-integer boundaries of x*2/pi, sin and cos branches coincide to O(1e-8)). No O(1) sine/cosine swap error exists anywhere in the domain.

rationale: The product x*(2/pi) is rounded to FP32 before the floor; near 65504 the product error can be ~4e-3, and the FP32-rounded 2/pi constant itself has ~6e-8 relative error that scales with x, so a boundary input can flip q by 1, swapping the sine/cosine branch.

scope_evidence.summary: EVERY finite FP16 value is legal, including both extrema +/-65504... Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6.

scope_rationale: The contract requires abs(actual[i]-sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for EVERY finite FP16 value, explicitly including the extrema ±65504, and states correctness is one verdict over the entire legal domain.
statement: For large |x| (e.g. a few thousand up to 65504), the FP32-rounded computation of q = floor(x*0.63661977236758134308 + 0.5) yields the wrong quadrant for some inputs where x*2/pi is near a half-integer, causing the kernel to evaluate cosine instead of sine (or vice versa) with error O(1), far above the 1e-6 absolute tolerance.

evidence.summary: Restricting to the 12284 large-|x| inputs (|x| >= 1024) where the kernel's q matches the exact FP64 q, cancellation in r_hi = x - q*1.5703125 is not catastrophic: max abs error vs FP64 reference is 1.34e-7 (worst at x=64512), zero violations of the 1e-6 tolerance. Because FP16 inputs are exactly representable in FP32 and q*1.5703125 is computed exactly for these magnitudes, the split-constant reduction stays accurate throughout the legal domain; the claimed ~1e-3-level cancellation error does not occur.

rationale: The split-constant scheme relies on x - q*C1 being computed exactly in FP32; but for |x| in the thousands the operands are large and the difference small, so the subtraction itself rounds, injecting up to ~2^-12-relative-of-|x| error directly into the argument, which the Taylor polynomial cannot cancel.

scope_evidence.summary: EVERY finite FP16 value is legal, including both extrema +/-65504... Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - sin(x[i])) <= 1e-6... Correctness is one verdict for the implementation, not per input.

scope_rationale: The contract demands 1e-6 absolute accuracy for all finite FP16 inputs including large magnitudes; the kernel uses FP32 intermediates, so a single-verdict correctness claim over the whole domain covers these inputs.
statement: For large |x|, the FP32 subtraction r_hi = x - q*1.5703125 suffers catastrophic cancellation: its rounding error can reach half an FP32 ulp of |x| (up to ~4e-3 near 65504), and that error flows into r and the polynomial, so the output deviates from sin(x) by amounts well above 1e-6 even when q is correct.
